name: Excavation Progress Report
summary: In Loch Modan, Ironband sends an excavation report to Thelsamar. Prospector Ironband asks you to carry his latest dispatches and renewed explosive supply orders to Jern Hornhelm.

sections.title: A Dispatch to Thelsamar
sections.body: Prospector Ironband's dig in Loch Modan depends on supplies from nearby settlements. Excavation takes picks, workers, and plenty of blasting powder to break through bedrock. Ironband sends runners with regular reports and supply requests to Jern Hornhelm, his local contact in Thelsamar.

sections.title: Missing Munitions
sections.body: When Jern Hornhelm receives Ironband's dispatch, he learns that aggressive troggs are harassing the dig. Powder could break stone or blast troggs, but Ironband's renewed request gives Hornhelm pause. He sent a large shipment weeks ago, and now wonders what happened to it along the rugged mountain paths.

faq.q: Who gives this report to you?
faq.answer: Prospector Ironband gives you the report at Ironband's Excavation Site in Loch Modan's southeastern hills. He supervises the archaeological dig there.
Jern Hornhelm is a dwarven Explorers' League contact in Thelsamar. He coordinates supplies and local logistics for archaeological expeditions across Loch Modan.

faq.q: Why does Prospector Ironband need more blastpowder?
aliases: what does ironband want powder for
faq.answer: Ironband needs blastpowder to clear solid rock for his excavation. The dig site is also swarming with hostile troggs, so explosives matter for defense as well.

faq.q: What happened to the previous shipment of powder?
faq.answer: Jern Hornhelm sent blastpowder weeks ago, but it never reached the excavation. Its disappearance points to trouble along the routes between Thelsamar and the outlying sites.

faq.q: What follows after delivering the progress report?
faq.answer: After reviewing Ironband's situation and the missing powder, Hornhelm sends you to report the expedition's status to his superiors in Ironforge.

faq.q: Why are troggs attacking the excavation site?
faq.answer: Dwarven excavations can uncover underground chambers and disturb trogg dens. Troggs see miners as intruders and swarm those digging into the earth.

angles.text: As a dwarf, you help Ironband pursue the Explorers' League's historical work and protect your kin from trogg attacks.
As a miner, you know reliable blasting powder is needed to break dense bedrock and tunnel into ancient strata.
As an Alliance member, you help keep supply lines open between Thelsamar and remote outposts across Loch Modan's mountains.
